name: discord_whoami
title: Show the bot's own identity and setup
description:
Reports which bot account the token belongs to, which servers it can reach, and the safety settings: destructive actions, @everyone pings and where files may be uploaded from.

Run this first to verify the server is configured correctly, or when a tool behaves unexpectedly.

annotations.title: Show the bot's own identity and setup

name: discord_list_guilds
title: List servers the bot is in
description:
Lists every server the bot has been invited to, with member counts.

Call this first when you are unsure which server to act on, or when another tool reports that the `guild` argument is ambiguous.

detail.description: compact returns only commonly needed fields (default, cheaper); full includes extra metadata.

annotations.title: List servers the bot is in

name: discord_get_guild
title: Get server details
description:
Returns an overview of one server: name, owner, member counts, creation date, enabled features, and how many channels and roles it has.

Useful as a first orientation step before doing anything else in an unfamiliar server.

name: discord_list_channels
title: List server channels
description:
Lists every channel in a server in the order Discord shows them, each tagged with its category.

Start here when you need a channel id or want to see how a server is organised. Filter with `type`; set include_threads to also list active threads.

name: discord_create_channel
title: Create a channel
description:
Creates a text, voice, category, announcement, stage, forum or media channel.

Nest it with `category` (create the category first if needed). `permissions` sets overwrites in the same request - e.g. a private staff channel: [{target:'@everyone', deny:['ViewChannel']}, {target:'Moderator', allow:['ViewChannel']}]. Without `permissions` a channel inside a category inherits the category's permissions.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

reason.description: Reason recorded in the audit log.

name: discord_edit_channel
title: Edit a channel
description:
Updates a channel's settings; only the fields you pass change.

Rename, set a topic, toggle NSFW, change slowmode or voice user limit, or move it: `category` moves it under a category, `category: null` moves it to the top level.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

name: discord_delete_channel
title: Delete a channel
description:
Permanently deletes a channel or thread and all of its messages. Cannot be undone.

Deleting a category does NOT delete the channels inside it; they move to the top level.

name: discord_manage_thread
title: Create or manage a thread or forum post
description:
Creates threads and changes their state.

- create: in a text channel pass `message_id` to branch off a message, or omit it for a standalone thread. In a forum channel this creates a post and `content` is its required first message.
- archive / unarchive / lock / unlock: change an existing thread's state.
- list: active threads in the server, or only under `channel` if given.

name: discord_set_channel_permissions
title: Set channel permission overwrites
description:
Grants or denies permissions for one role or member on a channel.

- Read-only for everyone: target='@everyone', deny=['SendMessages','AddReactions','CreatePublicThreads']
- Private channel: target='@everyone', deny=['ViewChannel'], then allow ViewChannel for the role that should see it

mode='merge' (default) changes only the listed permissions and keeps the rest of the existing overwrite; 'replace' makes allow/deny the whole overwrite; 'reset' removes the overwrite so everything inherits again.

A deny on @everyone applies to the bot too - grant the bot's role what it still needs there.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

Sets the top-to-bottom order of channels in one request.

Pass categories to order the categories, or channels that share one category to order those. Channels left out keep their place; the listed ones fill the slots they occupied, in the order given.

Voice channels always render below text channels in a category - Discord's rule, not changeable here.

Posts a message to a channel or thread: text, embeds, file uploads, polls and replies, or forwards an existing message (forward, on its own).

name: discord_read_messages
title: Read Discord message history
description:
Reads recent messages from a channel or thread, newest first (set oldest_first for reading order).

Fetches up to 500 by paging automatically. Text is clipped to 500 chars per message in compact mode; detail='full' allows 4000 and includes embed fields.

Without the MESSAGE CONTENT intent, content is empty for messages the bot did not send.

description:
Searches recent history across channels for text (message content and embed text).

Bots cannot use Discord's search index, so this scans the newest per_channel_limit messages of each channel (and active threads) in parallel. For older history page back with discord_read_messages.

Permanently deletes a message. Pass an array of message_ids to delete many at once - recent ones (< 14 days) go through Discord's bulk endpoint, 100 per request.

name: discord_list_roles
title: List server roles
description:
Lists every role in a server, highest first. detail='full' adds each role's permissions by name.

Position matters: a bot can only assign, edit or delete roles BELOW its own highest role. Check this listing first when a role operation fails with a permissions error.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

name: discord_manage_role
title: Create, edit or delete a role
description:
Manages roles themselves (use discord_manage_member_roles to assign them to people).

- create: needs `name`.
- edit: needs `role`, plus the fields to change.
- delete: needs `role`; destructive, requires DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

`permissions` takes names like ['ManageMessages','KickMembers']. A server holds at most 250 roles.

name: discord_reorder_roles
title: Reorder the role hierarchy
description:
Sets the vertical order of roles, highest first.

Order is not cosmetic: a role can only moderate, assign or edit roles BELOW it, and hoisted roles appear in the member list in this order.

Listed roles are placed directly below the bot's own highest role (Discord forbids a bot moving anything above itself); roles left out keep their relative order beneath them.

name: discord_moderate_member
title: Kick, ban, unban or time out a member
description:
Performs a moderation action on a member.

- kick: removes them; they can rejoin with an invite.
- ban: removes and blocks them; `delete_message_days` also purges their recent messages. An array of members is banned in one request.
- unban: lifts a ban (accepts the banned user's name).
- timeout: mutes them for `duration_minutes` (max 28 days). untimeout clears it.

kick, ban and timeout require DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true; unban and untimeout always work.

The bot's highest role must be ABOVE the target's. Always pass `reason` - it goes in the audit log.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

duration_minutes.description: Timeout length in minutes, max 40320 (28 days). Required for action='timeout'.

delete_message_days.description: For ban: also delete this many days of the user's recent messages (0-7).

name: discord_automod
title: Manage AutoMod rules
description:
Lists, creates, edits and deletes AutoMod rules that block, alert on or time out messages.

- list (default): every rule with its trigger, actions, exemptions and key settings.
- create: needs name and trigger (keyword, spam, keyword_preset or mention_spam). timeout only works with keyword or mention_spam.
- edit: needs rule and the fields to change; the trigger type cannot change.
- delete: needs rule; destructive, requires DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

Also destructive, each requiring DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true: disabling a rule (enabled=false), replacing its actions with ones that have no block or timeout, emptying a keyword rule's filter, and exempting @everyone.

`rule` takes an ID or an exact name.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

rule.description: Rule ID or exact name. Required for edit and delete.

name.description: Rule name. Required for create; new name when editing.

trigger.description: create only: what the rule looks for. A rule's trigger cannot be changed afterwards.

keywords.description: keyword rules: words or phrases to match, each up to 60 characters.

regex_patterns.description: keyword rules: regular expressions to match, up to 10.

allow_list.description: keyword and keyword_preset rules: words never blocked, each up to 60 characters (keyword: up to 100, keyword_preset: up to 1000).

presets.description: keyword_preset rules: built-in word lists to block.

mention_total_limit.description: mention_spam rules: most mentions one message may contain.

mention_raid_protection.description: mention_spam rules: also block raids where many new accounts mention people at once.

actions.description: What happens on a match. Defaults to a single block action on create.

type.description: block: stop the message. alert: post to a channel. timeout: mute the author.

custom_message.description: block only: text shown to the author.

channel.description: alert only: the channel that receives the alert.

duration_seconds.description: timeout only: seconds to mute the author, up to 2419200 (28 days).

exempt_roles.description: Roles the rule ignores, up to 20. Replaces the list.

exempt_channels.description: Channels the rule ignores, up to 50. Replaces the list.

items.description: Channel or thread: name ('general'), #mention or ID.

enabled.description: Turn the rule on or off. Defaults to on when created.

detail.description: compact returns only commonly needed fields (default, cheaper); full includes extra metadata.

name: discord_create_invite
title: Create an invite link
description:
Creates an invite link to a channel.

Defaults to a link that expires after 24 hours with unlimited uses, like Discord's own default. Set `max_age_seconds` (0 = never expires) or `max_uses` to change that, or `temporary` to grant membership only until the person disconnects.

name: discord_manage_invites
title: Manage invite links
description:
Lists the server's invite links and revokes them.

- list (default): every invite with its link, channel, inviter, uses and expiry. max_uses 0 means no limit.
- revoke: needs code, the code or a discord.gg / discord.com/invite link. Destructive: requires DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

Revoke works on any invite the bot can manage, so `guild` only matters for list.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

code.description: revoke only: the invite code, or a discord.gg or discord.com/invite link.

reason.description: Reason recorded in the audit log.

name: discord_scheduled_events
title: Manage scheduled events
description:
Lists, creates, edits and deletes server scheduled events, and lists who is interested in one.

- list (default): every event with status, times, location or channel, and interested count.
- create: needs name and start_time (in the future), plus location (external; also needs end_time) or channel (voice or stage).
- edit: needs event and the fields to change. Setting status to canceled is destructive and needs DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.
- users: needs event; paged with limit and after.
- delete: needs event; destructive, requires DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

`event` takes an ID or an exact name. Times are ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-01T18:00:00Z.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

event.description: Event ID or exact name. Required for edit, delete and users.

description.description: Event description, up to 1000 characters. When editing, '' clears it.

start_time.description: Start time, ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-01T18:00:00Z. Must be in the future.

end_time.description: End time, ISO 8601. Required for external events.

location.description: Where an external event takes place (up to 100 characters). Makes the event External.

channel.description: Voice or stage channel that hosts the event. Use instead of location.

status.description: edit only: move the event to another state. canceled is destructive and needs DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

limit.description: users only: how many to return per page.

after.description: users only: the last user ID from the previous page, to continue.

detail.description: compact returns only commonly needed fields (default, cheaper); full includes extra metadata.

reason.description: Reason recorded in the audit log.

name: discord_manage_emojis
title: Manage server emojis
description:
Lists, adds, renames and deletes custom server emojis.

- list (default): every emoji with its ID and a ready-to-send mention.
- create: needs name (2-32 letters, digits or _) and file ({path} or {url}; PNG, JPG, GIF or WebP, max 256 KiB). roles restricts who can use it.
- rename: needs emoji and name. delete: needs emoji; destructive, requires DISCORD_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

`emoji` takes an ID, '<:name:id>' or the name.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

name: discord_wait_for_event
title: Wait for a live Discord event
description:
Blocks until a matching live event arrives, or the timeout expires - a reply in a channel, someone joining, a reaction.

The first call opens a gateway connection (a few seconds); later calls reuse it. Pass after_seq from a previous discord_recent_events result to also catch anything that arrived in between. Keep timeout_seconds modest - the call is held open for its whole duration.

types.description: Event types to wait for, e.g. ['MESSAGE_CREATE'].

guild.description: Only match events from this server.

channel.description: Only events in this channel, or in any of these channels.

from_author.description: Only events caused by this username or user ID.

after_seq.description: Only events newer than this seq (from a previous result's last_seq), so nothing is seen twice or missed.

include_raw.description: Include the full raw gateway payload. Verbose.

name: discord_recent_events
title: Read buffered live events
description:
Returns events buffered since the gateway connected, without waiting.

The buffer fills only while connected - from the first call to this tool or discord_wait_for_event until an idle period passes. Pass after_seq (the last_seq from the previous call) to get only new events, oldest first, so repeated calls page through everything. For older history use discord_read_messages.

guild.description: Server name or ID. Optional if the bot is in one server or a default is set.

channel.description: Only events in this channel, or in any of these channels.

name: discord_batch
title: Run several Discord tools in parallel
description:
Runs several different Discord tool calls in one request, in parallel within Discord's rate limits.

Each operation is {tool, args} with exactly the arguments that tool takes directly. `defaults` fills arguments an operation leaves out (e.g. {guild: 'my server'}), wherever the tool accepts them. For the same tool over many targets, prefer passing an array to that tool instead.

One failure does not stop the others - each operation reports ok/error - unless stop_on_error is set.

Example: operations: [{"tool":"discord_send_message","args":{"channel":"general","content":"Deploy done"}}, {"tool":"discord_manage_member_roles","args":{"member":"alice","add":["Release"]}}]

tool.description: Name of the tool to run, e.g. 'discord_send_message'.

defaults.description: Arguments applied to every operation that accepts them and does not set them itself.

concurrency.description: How many operations run at once. Defaults to DISCORD_BATCH_CONCURRENCY (4).

stop_on_error.description: Abandon operations that have not started once one fails, including a fan-out where any item failed. In-flight work still completes.

annotations.title: Run several Discord tools in parallel
